zh.summary: Palma.ai 为企业提供面向 MCP 工具与 Skill 的统一治理层，通过单一连接器把身份、权限、参数级策略、人工审批与审计串成一条受控路径。
zh.judgment: 它押注的不是某个 AI 助手，而是企业采用 MCP 后必然出现的“谁能用哪个工具、以什么参数、由谁批准”的治理缺口；成败取决于能否在客户自有基础设施中快速落地并被审计方接受。
zh.replaces: 替代企业目前用零散 MCP 网关、手工配置的 API 密钥、分散在各助手中的权限设置以及事后人工翻日志的临时做法。
zh.segment: 企业 AI Agent 治理与 MCP 网关
zh.product: 官网把产品描述为“每个 Agent 与每个工具之间的一层策略层”：所有 MCP 服务器和 Skill 通过一个连接器下发，按 IdP 组分配，并跟随用户进入 Claude、ChatGPT、Copilot、Cursor 等不同客户端。能力范围包括参数级策略判断、高风险调用的人工审批与法定人数、PII 与密钥在传输中脱敏、可离线验证的防篡改审计并推送到 SIEM，以及带版本和扫描的 Skill 与 Pack。部署形态声称支持本地、VPC 乃至完全气隙环境，但平台地图页需要提交企业邮箱才能查看，具体功能边界尚无法从公开文本完整核实。
zh.customer: 使用者是已经让员工用多种 AI 助手调用内部系统（如 Salesforce、Slack、GitHub、Snowflake）的企业 IT、安全与合规团队；付费者通常是 IT 或安全预算的负责人。痛点是员工各自接入 MCP 工具导致权限失控、敏感数据外泄、高风险操作无人批准、事后无法向审计证明“谁让哪个 Agent 做了什么”，这类审查在每次新工具上线和季度审计时反复出现。
zh.workflow: 典型流程是：管理员在 Entra、Okta 或任意 OIDC 提供方中按组授权，用户打开任意受支持的助手即获得对应连接器；Agent 发起工具调用时，请求先经过身份与权限校验，再对实际参数（渠道、金额、字段）执行策略，命中高风险规则则暂停并通知指定审批人；通过后凭据从企业 vault 临时换取，PII 在到达工具前被脱敏，最终把调用归属、参数、结果、耗时与成本写入防篡改审计。Skill 则以不可变版本发布，扫描通过后才被提供给 Agent。
zh.business_model: 输入未披露定价页，因此无法确认是按席位、按调用量还是按部署实例收费，也不能写成免费或订阅。可推断（非已验证）其企业本地/VPC 部署形态更接近年度企业合同加实施服务，单位经济取决于单客户部署与运维成本能否被合同规模覆盖；气隙与自托管会抬高交付成本，需靠较大席位基数摊薄。
zh.traction: 可确认的采用信号有限：投资方 D11Z 与 Plug and Play 在官网被引述为既是投资方又是客户，属于公司披露的自我陈述，不构成独立审计的客户数或留存证据。官网展示的成功率、调用量、成本等数字是产品界面示意，不能当作真实运营指标。缺少公开客户案例、定价、文档与第三方评测，无法判断实际部署规模与续费情况。
zh.moat: 与直接使用通用模型或各家助手自带权限相比，Palma 的差异在于跨客户端的统一策略与可离线验证的审计，且建立在开放 MCP 标准与客户自有基础设施上，降低锁定顾虑。壁垒条件是：策略引擎对真实参数语义的判断足够准确、与 IdP 和 SIEM 的集成足够深、以及审计证据被外部审计方认可；若这些只是薄封装，通用网关或云厂商原生治理功能可以快速覆盖。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 pre-seed，金额与原币由确定性层给出，投资方名单不等于领投名单。该阶段说明公司已把“企业级 MCP 治理”讲成可演示的产品叙事并获得早期机构与战略投资方支持，但不证明需求验证、收入或留存。资金用途未披露；下一里程碑应是从演示走向可核查的生产部署、公开定价与至少一个可引用的客户案例。
zh.risks: 第一，若企业客户不愿把治理层部署在自有基础设施，或部署周期远超“数周”的宣称，销售周期与交付成本会吞噬早期资金。第二，若 MCP 生态或主要助手平台把权限、审批与审计内建为标准能力，Palma 的中间层价值被压缩。第三，策略误判导致合法调用被阻断或敏感调用被放行，会直接摧毁安全团队的信任。第四，审计证据若不被外部审计方接受，核心卖点失效。
zh.takeaway: 可借鉴之处是把治理做成“默认最优路径”而非附加审批：一次授权随身份组流动、跨客户端复用，并用可离线验证的审计把合规成本转化为销售理由。对创业者而言，选择一个标准正在形成、但平台方尚未内建治理的缝隙，并以客户自有基础设施部署来化解数据外流顾虑，是合理的切入方式。
zh.watch_next: 下一步应观察：是否公开定价与部署文档；是否出现可独立核验的客户案例与部署时长；D11Z、Plug and Play 之外的付费客户数量；以及主要 AI 助手平台是否推出原生 MCP 权限与审计功能，从而改变竞争格局。

en.summary: Palma.ai offers enterprises a central governance layer for MCP tools and Skills, routing every agent through one connector that enforces identity, entitlement, argument-level policy, human approval and audit.
en.judgment: It is betting on the governance gap that appears once enterprises adopt MCP—who may use which tool, with which arguments, approved by whom—rather than on any single assistant; success hinges on fast deployment inside customer infrastructure and acceptance by auditors.
en.replaces: It replaces ad-hoc MCP gateways, hand-managed API keys, permissions scattered across individual assistants, and after-the-fact log reading that enterprises use today.
en.segment: Enterprise AI agent governance and MCP gateway
en.product: The site describes a policy layer between every agent and every tool: all MCP servers and Skills are delivered through a single connector, assigned by IdP group, and follow the user into Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor and other clients. Capabilities include argument-level policy decisions, human approval with quorum for high-risk calls, PII and secret redaction on the wire, tamper-evident audit verifiable offline and streamed to SIEM, plus versioned and scanned Skills and Packs. Deployment is claimed for on-prem, VPC and fully air-gapped environments, though the platform map requires a business email, so the full functional boundary cannot be verified from public text.
en.customer: Users are enterprise IT, security and compliance teams whose employees already call internal systems such as Salesforce, Slack, GitHub and Snowflake from multiple AI assistants; the payer is typically the owner of the IT or security budget. The recurring pain is uncontrolled permissions as employees wire up MCP tools themselves, sensitive data leakage, high-risk actions with no approver, and an inability to prove to auditors who let which agent do what—a review that repeats with every new tool and every quarterly audit.
en.workflow: An admin grants access by group in Entra, Okta or any OIDC provider, and a user opening any supported assistant receives the matching connector. When an agent issues a tool call, the request first passes identity and entitlement checks, then policy on the actual arguments (channel, amount, fields); if a high-risk rule matches, the call pauses and notifies a named approver. On approval, credentials are brokered from the enterprise vault, PII is redacted before reaching the tool, and the call's attribution, arguments, result, duration and cost are written to a tamper-evident audit trail. Skills are published as immutable, scanner-passed versions before being served to agents.
en.business_model: No pricing page was captured, so it is unknown whether Palma charges per seat, per call or per deployment instance; it must not be described as free or subscription-based. A conditional inference (not verified) is that on-prem/VPC deployment lends itself to annual enterprise contracts plus implementation services, with unit economics depending on whether contract size covers deployment and operations cost; air-gapped and self-hosted delivery raises delivery cost and needs a large seat base to amortize.
en.traction: Verifiable adoption signals are limited: D11Z and Plug and Play are quoted on the site as both investors and customers, which is a company-reported claim and not independently audited evidence of customer count or retention. Success rates, call volumes and cost figures shown on the site are product-interface illustrations, not real operating metrics. Public customer cases, pricing, documentation and third-party reviews are missing, so actual deployment scale and renewals cannot be judged.
en.moat: Compared with using general models or each assistant's built-in permissions, Palma's differentiation is cross-client unified policy and offline-verifiable audit, built on the open MCP standard and inside customer infrastructure to reduce lock-in concerns. The moat holds only if the policy engine judges real argument semantics accurately, integrations with IdP and SIEM are deep, and audit evidence is accepted by external auditors; if it is a thin wrapper, generic gateways or native cloud governance features can close the gap quickly.
en.funding_read: This is a pre-seed round; amount and currency are rendered by the deterministic layer, and the investor list is not a lead-investor list. The stage indicates the company has turned enterprise MCP governance into a demonstrable product narrative and attracted early institutional and strategic backers, but it does not prove demand validation, revenue or retention. Use of funds is undisclosed; the next milestone should be moving from demo to verifiable production deployments, public pricing and at least one citable customer case.
en.risks: First, if enterprises resist deploying the governance layer in their own infrastructure or deployment takes far longer than the claimed weeks, sales cycles and delivery cost will consume early capital. Second, if the MCP ecosystem or major assistant platforms build permissions, approvals and audit in as standard features, Palma's middle layer is squeezed. Third, policy misjudgment that blocks legitimate calls or lets sensitive calls through would directly destroy security-team trust. Fourth, if audit evidence is not accepted by external auditors, the core selling point fails.
en.takeaway: A transferable practice is to make governance the default best path rather than an added approval step: authorize once by identity group, reuse across clients, and turn compliance cost into a sales argument with offline-verifiable audit. For founders, entering a gap where a standard is forming but platform owners have not yet built governance, and deploying inside customer infrastructure to defuse data-egress concerns, is a reasonable wedge.
en.watch_next: Watch whether pricing and deployment documentation become public; whether independently verifiable customer cases and deployment timelines appear; the number of paying customers beyond D11Z and Plug and Play; and whether major assistant platforms ship native MCP permission and audit features that change the competitive landscape.

Common Questions Quick answers about Palma.ai's enterprise MCP platform What is Palma.ai in one sentence? Palma.ai is the enterprise governance layer for MCP — it gives every person and agent a single governed connector carrying the tools and Skills they're entitled to, enforces policies on the actual arguments of a call, pauses high-risk actions for approval, and records everything in a tamper-evident audit trail. What does MCP governance mean? Deciding which person may use which tool, with which arguments, with whose approval — and being able to prove it afterwards. MCP itself covers how a client authenticates to a server and how a tool is described and called; it does not decide which person may use which tool, hold a risky call for a human, or keep the record an auditor asks for. Palma adds that layer: one governed connector per person, assigned by identity-provider group, carrying the tools and Skills they are entitled to into whichever assistant they already use. Does my team have to set up MCP servers themselves? No. Connectors are assigned by IdP group through Entra or Okta, so a joiner gets theirs on day one and a leaver loses it the moment the group changes. Every MCP server your team approves arrives through that same connector — no per-user install, no config files, no credentials sitting on a laptop. What's a Skill, and why does it matter? A tool is a verb — "send an email". A Skill is the playbook that tells an agent when and how to use the verbs it already has: how your team actually closes the books, runs an incident review, or qualifies a lead. Skills are versioned, scanned before they're served, and scoped like any other piece of enterprise software — so your best operator's process reaches everyone else's agent. Does it work with the AI clients we already use? Yes — everything is served over MCP, so the same connector, Skills and policies follow the person into whichever assistant they open, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor or something else. Switching tools doesn't mean re-approving, re-installing or re-auditing anything. How do we prove what an agent actually did? Every tool call is attributed to the person it was done for, the agent that did it, and the application it ran in — with the arguments, result, duration and cost. The audit trail is tamper-evident and verifiable offline with your own key, so your auditor doesn't have to take our word for it, and it streams to the SIEM you already run. How is Palma.ai deployed — SaaS, on-prem, VPC? Palma.ai is designed for enterprise environments: typically VPC or on-prem, including fully air-gapped, depending on your regulatory and security needs. The MCP layer and governance plane run on your infrastructure, so sensitive business data doesn't have to move into multi-tenant SaaS. We can also host it for you if you prefer.
